tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.
tools.name: send_message

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-5.6-sol`: Older generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.
tools.name: spawn_agent

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.
tools.name: wait_agent

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.
tools.name: mcp__cua_repl

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

# FORGE v4 — Persistent Router Agent System

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-15

Phase 2 backend implementation and acceptance are in progress. The last fully
archived V27 suite recorded **1,878 passed tests and 2 failures**; its three
strict live scenarios did not pass. Those results remain historical evidence.
The current work removes cumulative token limits at the user's request and
adds source-bound memory handoffs, lossless source framing and context
compaction informed by the open-source Codex implementation. Current-source
full tests and real-provider completion have not yet been established.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical and model semantic recall, and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. Bounded feedback-driven remaining-DAG proposals are implemented; their general quality, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain subject to recorded acceptance. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

Python 3.11+ recommended.

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# macOS/Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt
python -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
pytest
python -m forge_api
```

The lock file is verified on Windows with Python 3.13; other platforms and Python versions have not been verified. The editable installation requires build tooling already available. API documentation endpoints are disabled.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.

### Approved Worker execution

`python_test` runs bounded pure Python function tests against a governed workspace
file using an isolated subprocess and an AST interpreter. Its approved parameters
are `path`, `function` and `suite.cases` (1–32 input/expected cases). It supports
bounded loops, helpers and recursion; imports, attributes, external calls, file or
network access, and arbitrary shell/pytest execution are unavailable. A failed
case records the actual and expected values in a failed immutable receipt. An
approved Worker can use `file_revise` on its own artifact, rerun the tests and
submit the new evidence within its original repair and resource limits. No new
dependency or environment variable is required.

Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. File writes additionally require a workspace grant; HTTPS/MCP actions require exact action approval and an operator allowlist. `FORGE_TOOL_NETWORK_HOSTS_JSON` is a JSON host list (at most 64); `FORGE_MCP_SERVERS_JSON` maps server names to `{"url":"https://example.invalid/mcp","tools":["example_tool"]}` (at most 16 servers), with the HTTPS host included in the allowlist. Defaults are empty and deny network access. These values are operator configuration, never model output. `jsonschema` validates Worker result contracts; it does not judge domain correctness. Unsupported or failed fixed JSON criteria require manual review; infrastructure verification retries are bounded to three attempts.

A member's `input_tokens + output_tokens` defines its cumulative Worker/review

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose autonomous Agent desktop application.

Phase 2 backend implementation and acceptance are in progress. The last fully

compaction informed by the open-source Codex implementation. Current-source

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).

microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. **The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. Codex, DSH and Claude Code are architectural references only, never execution backends.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering foundation with bounded context recovery, sourced lexical and model semantic recall, and evidence-gated execution. The Router uses a configured Provider or explicitly fails. Mock tests, synthetic experiments and real-provider observations are identified separately. The current independent reviewer uses the approved Worker's model in a fresh context. Bounded feedback-driven remaining-DAG proposals are implemented; their general quality, arbitrary-scale continuity and complex-task correctness remain subject to recorded acceptance. Plan/team/replacement approval stays authenticated and Review mode remains enabled. A proposal record alone never proves execution.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

```bash
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
# Windows PowerShell:
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt

python -m forge_api
```

The lock file is verified on Windows with Python 3.13; other platforms and Python versions have not been verified. The editable installation requires build tooling already available. API documentation endpoints are disabled.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. The first successful open migrates it in place to the current schema without changing the Router ID or existing records. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. External tool effects require their own durable intents and receipts; event delivery alone does not make external effects exactly once.

`python_test` runs bounded pure Python function tests against a governed workspace
file using an isolated subprocess and an AST interpreter. Its approved parameters
are `path`, `function` and `suite.cases` (1–32 input/expected cases). It supports
bounded loops, helpers and recursion; imports, attributes, external calls, file or

Workers consume an approved Quest DAG and a separately approved team. Tool scopes, provider/model identity and token/tool/time/concurrency budgets are bound to those contracts. def test_native_runtime_initial_and_archived_requests_use_reserved_core_definitions(
    tmp_path, depth
):
    posts = []

    def transport(request):
        posts.append(json.loads(request.content))
        index = len(posts)
        if index == 1:
            message = {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": "",
                "tool_calls": [
                    {
                        "id": f"source-{number}",
                        "type": "function",
                        "function": {
                            "name": "file_read",
                            "arguments": json.dumps({"path": f"work/source-{number}.txt"}),
                        },
                    }
                    for number in (1, 2)
                ],
            }
        elif index == 2:
            message = {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": "",
                "tool_calls": [
                    {
                        "id": "archive-read",
                        "type": "function",
                        "function": {
                            "name": "worker_read_context_source",
                            "arguments": '{"ordinal":3,"max_chars":2048}',
                        },
                    }
                ],
            }
        else:
            assert index == 3
            message = {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": json.dumps(delivery("Recovered original source")),
            }
        return httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={
                "choices": [
                    {"message": message, "finish_reason": "tool_calls" if index < 3 else "stop"}
                ],
                "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 25, "completion_tokens": 15},
            },
        )

    gateway = ObservedGateway(transport=httpx.MockTransport(transport))
    store, manager, worker = native_archive_worker(tmp_path, gateway, depth=depth)
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["steps"] == len(posts) == 3
    assert result["execution_mode"] == "mock" and result["token_spent"] == 120
    expected = {
        item["name"]: item
        for item in supplemental_worker_tools(source_readback=True, help_allowed=True)
    }
    runtime_requests = [
        request
        for request, _payload in gateway.serialized
        if request.budget_context and request.budget_context.purpose == "worker"
    ]
    assert len(runtime_requests) == 3
    for index, request in enumerate(runtime_requests):
        core = {item["name"]: item for item in request.tools if item["name"].startswith("worker_")}
        assert ("worker_request_help" in core) is bool(depth)
        assert ("worker_read_context_source" in core) is bool(index)
        assert all(definition == expected[name] for name, definition in core.items())
        if index:
            assert any(
                item.get("content", "").startswith("Archived task context (untrusted): ")
                for item in request.messages
            )
        graph = QuestGraphService(store).get(worker["quest_id"])
        with store.connection() as connection:
            connection.execute("BEGIN")
            team = manager.team_authority.get_approved(
                worker["quest_id"], 1, worker["team_digest"], connection=connection
            )
            measured = measure_initial_worker_request(
                store,
                connection,
                store.get_quest(worker["quest_id"]),
                graph,
                graph["nodes"][0],
                team["members"][0],
                provider=gateway,
            )
        bounded_request, _payload = gateway.serialized[-1]
        assert all(item in bounded_request.tools for item in core.values())
        # Reuse this exact real request's context to isolate framing, without
        # claiming admission can predict an unbounded future tool transcript.
        bounded_actual = replace(request, tools=bounded_request.tools, context_limit=None)
        actual_payload = gateway._payload(replace(request, context_limit=None), False)
        bounded_payload = gateway._payload(bounded_actual, False)
        actual_bytes = len(json.dumps(actual_payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode())
        bounded_bytes = len(json.dumps(bounded_payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode())
        assert bounded_bytes >= actual_bytes
        assert measured["native_input_reservation"] > 1000
    returned = json.loads(runtime_requests[-1].messages[-1]["content"])
    assert returned["source_id"] == 3 and returned["complete"] is False
    assert "中文 original source 1" in returned["content"]
"""Typed delivery feedback with unchanged approval/budget gates; no network."""

import asyncio
import copy
import hashlib
import json

import pytest
from test_review_envelope_phase2 import envelope, new_pending
from test_worker_intelligence_phase2 import delivery, prepared, response

from forge_core.domain import DomainError
from forge_core.review_envelope import review_cycle_state
from forge_core.worker_envelope import (
    DeliveryCapacityError,
    canonical,
    cycle_allowance,
    validate_delivery,
)
from forge_core.worker_prompts import initial_worker_messages
from forge_core.worker_runtime import _delivery_schema_diagnostics
from forge_core.worker_schema import STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA


def rejection_events(store):
    return [
        json.loads(event["payload"])
        for event in store.list_events(limit=100)
        if event["event_type"] == "worker.model_response_rejected"
    ]


def feedback(model):
    return json.loads(model.requests[-1].messages[-1]["content"])["repair_request"]["detail"]


def test_delivery_capacity_error_counts_exact_canonical_utf8_including_escaping():
    value = delivery('中文 "quotes" \\ newline\n')
    actual = len(canonical(value).encode("utf-8"))
    contract = {"review_envelope": {"max_delivery_bytes": actual}}
    assert validate_delivery(contract, value) is None
    contract["review_envelope"]["max_delivery_bytes"] -= 1
    with pytest.raises(DeliveryCapacityError) as caught:
        validate_delivery(contract, value)
    assert isinstance(caught.value, ValueError)
    assert caught.value.code == "delivery_byte_bound"
    assert caught.value.actual_bytes == actual and caught.value.max_bytes == actual - 1
    assert "中文" not in str(caught.value)


def test_legacy_delivery_without_capacity_contract_retains_existing_behavior():
    assert validate_delivery({}, delivery("x" * 100000)) is None


def test_delivery_bound_feedback_reports_numbers_and_preserves_reserved_review_cycle(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    value = delivery("x" * 2500)
    env = envelope(max_delivery_bytes=1024)
    original = copy.deepcopy(env)
    store, manager, model, worker = new_pending(
        tmp_path,
        monkeypatch,
        env=env,
        responses=[response(value), response(delivery())],
        budget=100000,
    )
    detail = feedback(model)
    assert detail["code"] == "delivery_byte_bound"
    assert detail["actual_bytes"] == len(canonical(value).encode("utf-8"))
    assert detail["max_bytes"] == 1024 and detail["schema_errors"] == []
    assert "not valid JSON" not in detail["message"]
    assert detail["response_sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(response(value).text.encode()).hexdigest()
    assert env == original
    after = manager.get(worker["id"])
    assert after["repairs"] == 1 and after["steps"] == 2 and after["token_spent"] == 80
    assert after["token_limit"] == 100000 and after["state"] == "review_pending"
    with store.connection() as connection:
        cycle = review_cycle_state(connection, after["id"], env)
        # The initial self-repair consumed the shared correction call, while
        # both independent reviews remain reserved within the original limit.
        assert cycle["reviews_remaining"] == 2 and cycle["correction_calls_remaining"] == 0
        assert cycle["future_reserve_tokens"] == 34048 and cycle["correction_started"]
        with pytest.raises(DomainError, match="correction call count exhausted"):
            cycle_allowance(connection, after, env)
        assert (
            connection.execute(
                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE event_type='review.result'"
            ).fetchone()[0]
            == 0
        )
    events = rejection_events(store)
    assert len(events) == 1 and events[0]["reason_code"] == "delivery_byte_bound"
    assert events[0]["diagnostics"] == detail


def test_size_and_schema_errors_are_reported_together_without_echoing_values(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    marker = "PRIVATE_MODEL_VALUE_MARKER"
    value = delivery("x" * 2200)
    value["findings"] = marker
    store, _manager, model, _worker = new_pending(
        tmp_path,
        monkeypatch,
        env=envelope(max_delivery_bytes=1024),
        responses=[response(value), response(delivery())],
        budget=100000,
    )
    detail = feedback(model)
    assert detail["code"] == "delivery_byte_bound"
    assert {"validator": "type", "path": ["findings"]} in detail["schema_errors"]
    assert marker not in json.dumps(detail) and marker not in json.dumps(rejection_events(store))


def test_json_syntax_failure_has_position_without_capacity_misclassification(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    store, _manager, model, _worker = new_pending(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch, responses=[response('{"summary":'), response(delivery())]
    )
    detail = feedback(model)
    assert detail["code"] == "invalid_json_syntax"
    assert detail["line"] == 1 and detail["column"] > 0 and detail["position"] > 0
    assert "actual_bytes" not in detail and "schema_errors" not in detail
    assert rejection_events(store)[0]["reason_code"] == "invalid_json_syntax"


def test_small_parsed_schema_failure_is_not_reported_as_invalid_json(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    value = delivery()
    value["findings"] = "PRIVATE_MODEL_VALUE_MARKER"
    store, _manager, model, _worker = new_pending(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch, responses=[response(value), response(delivery())], budget=100000
    )
    detail = feedback(model)
    assert detail["code"] == "output_schema"
    assert detail["schema_errors"] == [{"validator": "type", "path": ["findings"]}]
    assert "PRIVATE_MODEL_VALUE_MARKER" not in json.dumps(detail)
    assert rejection_events(store)[0]["reason_code"] == "output_schema"


def test_nonfinite_parsed_value_is_distinguished_from_json_syntax(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    value = delivery()
    value["confidence"] = float("nan")
    _store, _manager, model, _worker = new_pending(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch, responses=[response(value), response(delivery())], budget=100000
    )
    assert feedback(model)["code"] == "invalid_json_value"
    assert feedback(model)["validation_stage"] == "canonical_json"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("violation", ["missing_fields", "confidence"])
def test_legacy_schema_delivery_review_failures_are_contract_errors(tmp_path, violation):
    value = {"summary": "Incomplete"} if violation == "missing_fields" else delivery()
    if violation == "confidence":
        value["confidence"] = 2
    _store, manager, model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, [response(value), response(delivery())])
    result = asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))
    assert result["state"] == "review_pending" and result["repairs"] == 1
    detail = feedback(model)
    assert detail["code"] == "invalid_output_contract"
    assert detail["validation_stage"] == "delivery_review"
    assert "finite canonical JSON" not in detail["message"]
    if violation == "missing_fields":
        assert set(detail["missing_fields"]) == set(delivery()) - {"summary"}
    else:
        assert detail["missing_fields"] == [] and detail["path"] == ["confidence"]


def test_post_canonical_value_error_is_not_reported_as_serialization_failure(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    from forge_core import worker_envelope

    original = worker_envelope.validate_delivery
    calls = 0

    def check_contract(capsule, value):
        nonlocal calls
        calls += 1
        if calls == 1:
            raise ValueError("PRIVATE_CONTRACT_ERROR_MARKER")
        return original(capsule, value)

    monkeypatch.setattr(worker_envelope, "validate_delivery", check_contract)
    store, _manager, model, _worker = new_pending(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch, responses=[response(delivery()), response(delivery())], budget=100000
    )
    detail = feedback(model)
    assert detail["code"] == "invalid_output_contract"
    assert detail["validation_stage"] == "capacity_contract"
    assert "finite canonical JSON" not in detail["message"]
    assert "PRIVATE_CONTRACT_ERROR_MARKER" not in json.dumps(detail)
    assert rejection_events(store)[0]["reason_code"] == "invalid_output_contract"


def test_schema_diagnostics_are_bounded_and_omit_unknown_field_names():
    marker = "PRIVATE_MODEL_VALUE_MARKER"
    value = {marker: marker, "summary": 3, "findings": marker, "confidence": 3}
    diagnostics = _delivery_schema_diagnostics(value, STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA)
    assert len(diagnostics) == 3
    assert marker not in json.dumps(diagnostics)
    assert len(json.dumps(diagnostics).encode()) < 1024


def prompt_contract(*, bounded):
    contract = {
        "constraints": {"allowed_tools": []},
        "responsibility": "Inspect the source",
        "input_contract": ["Approved source"],
        "output_schema": STRICT_DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA,
        "acceptance_criteria": ["delivery_review"],

    }
    if bounded:

@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_successors", [False, True])
def test_exact_capacity_prompt_precedes_intermediate_size_guidance(has_successors):
    contract = prompt_contract(bounded=True)
    before = copy.deepcopy(contract)
    messages = initial_worker_messages(contract, has_successors=has_successors)
    policy = messages[0]["content"]

    assert "4 KiB" not in policy and "6 KiB" not in policy
    assert "one shared evidence list" in policy and "Preserve all assigned requirements" in policy
    assert contract == before


def test_legacy_intermediate_prompt_keeps_its_existing_writing_guidance():
    policy = initial_worker_messages(prompt_contract(bounded=False), has_successors=True)[0][
        "content"
    ]
    assert "4 KiB" in policy and "6 KiB" in policy

"""Offline capacity diagnostics with actual approvals, receipts and revisions."""

import asyncio
import hashlib
import json

import pytest
import test_worker_report_guidance_phase2 as reports
from test_worker_intelligence_phase2 import delivery, response, tool

from forge_core.governance import GovernanceService
from forge_core.independent_review import (
    IndependentReviewService,
    _hash,
    _json,
    _packet,
    _ReviewBoundaryError,
    review_pass_matches,
)
from forge_core.store import Store
from forge_core.team_composition import TeamCompositionService
from forge_core.tool_engine import ToolEngine
from forge_core.worker_runtime import WorkerManager

PASS = {"verdict": "PASS", "findings": [], "revision_goals": [], "confidence": 0.8}


def pending(
    tmp_path,
    monkeypatch,
    *,
    successor=True,
    downstream_writer=True,
    revise=True,
    source_bytes=23400,
    source_reads=1,
    explanation_repeats=2000,
    context_window=64000,
    raw_oversize=True,
):
    propose_plan = reports.QuestGraphService.propose
    propose_team = reports.TeamCompositionService.propose
    model_profile = reports.ModelProfile
    input_tokens = min(56000, context_window - 4000)

    def plan(self, quest_id, proposal, **kwargs):
        if revise:
            proposal["nodes"][0]["allowed_tools"].append("file_revise")
        if successor and downstream_writer:
            proposal["nodes"][1].update(
                objective="Author the final integrated findings artifact using the reviewed research.",
                expected_artifact="work/final.json",
                success_criteria=["json_review:work/final.json"],
                allowed_tools=["file_read", "file_write"],
            )
        return propose_plan(self, quest_id, proposal, **kwargs)

    def team(self, quest_id, roles, limits, **kwargs):
        for role in roles:
            role["input_tokens"] = input_tokens
        if revise:
            if "file_revise" not in roles[0]["tools"]:
                roles[0]["tools"].append("file_revise")
            limits["allowed_tools"].append("file_revise")
        limits["max_total_tokens"] = (input_tokens + 3000) * len(roles)
        return propose_team(self, quest_id, roles, limits, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(reports.QuestGraphService, "propose", plan)
    monkeypatch.setattr(reports.TeamCompositionService, "propose", team)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        reports,
        "ModelProfile",
        lambda **fields: model_profile(**{**fields, "context_window": context_window}),
    )
    source = ("evidence " * ((source_bytes + 8) // 9))[:source_bytes]
    content = {
        "finding": "A precise evidenced finding required by the next node.",
        "citation": {
            "source_path": "work/input.txt",
            "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest(),
        },
        "explanation": "Repeated explanation. " * explanation_repeats,
    }
    store, manager, model, worker, _ = reports.approved_report(
        tmp_path,
        criterion="json_review:work/findings.json",
        files={"work/findings.json": _json(content)},
        successor=successor,
        source=source,
    )
    model.responses[1:1] = [
        tool("file_read", {"path": "work/input.txt"}, ordinal=20 + index)
        for index in range(source_reads - 1)
    ]
    assert asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))["state"] == "review_pending"
    with store.connection() as connection:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        row = connection.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)).fetchone()
        if raw_oversize:
            with pytest.raises(_ReviewBoundaryError) as caught:
                _packet(store, connection, row)
            assert caught.value.code == "review_packet_too_large"
            packet = caught.value.packet
        else:
            packet = _packet(store, connection, row)
    return store, manager, model, worker, packet, content


def events(store, kind):
    return [
        json.loads(row["payload"])
        for row in store.list_events(limit=1000)
        if row["event_type"] == kind
    ]


def test_capacity_feedback_preserves_rejected_packet_and_never_claims_model_review(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    store, manager, model, worker, packet, _ = pending(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    before = manager.get(worker["id"])
    original = _json(packet)
    service = IndependentReviewService(manager)
    result = asyncio.run(service.review(worker["id"]))
    after = manager.get(worker["id"])
    assert result["verdict"] == "NEEDS_REVISION" and result["revision_applied"]
    assert result["review_context"] == "deterministic_review_capacity"
    assert result["validation_source"] == "core_review_capacity"
    assert result["packet_sha256"] == _hash(packet) and _json(packet) == original
    assert result["capacity_diagnostics"]["raw_packet_bytes"] == len(original.encode()) > 65536
    assert result["capacity_diagnostics"]["raw_packet_cap"] == 65536
    assert "call_id" not in result and "provider_id" not in result
    assert len(model.requests) == 3 and not events(store, "review.started")
    assert after["state"] == "queued" and after["repairs"] == 1
    for key in ("steps", "tool_spent", "token_spent", "token_limit", "tool_limit", "step_limit"):
        assert after[key] == before[key]
    assert "Preserve ALL assigned requirements" in result["revision_goals"][0]
    assert f"{len(original.encode())}/65536" in result["revision_goals"][0]
    with store.connection() as connection:
        assert service._rounds(connection, worker["id"]) == 1
        assert connection.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM action_receipts").fetchone()[0] == 2
        assert not review_pass_matches(store, connection, after, "json_review:work/findings.json")


def test_compact_complete_owned_revision_still_requires_fresh_model_review(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    store, manager, model, worker, packet, content = pending(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    service = IndependentReviewService(manager)
    assert asyncio.run(service.review(worker["id"]))["revision_applied"]
    artifact = packet["artifacts"][0]
    compact = {**content, "explanation": "Repeated explanation."}
    model.responses.extend(
        [
            tool(
                "file_revise",
                {
                    "path": "work/findings.json",
                    "prior_receipt_id": artifact["receipt_id"],
                    "expected_sha256": artifact["sha256"],
                    "content": _json(compact),
                },
                ordinal=10,
            ),
            response(delivery("Complete compact findings, with all original evidence.")),
            response(PASS),
        ]
    )
    assert asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))["state"] == "review_pending"
    assert len(model.requests) == 5 and len(events(store, "review.result")) == 1
    result = asyncio.run(service.review(worker["id"]))
    assert result["verdict"] == "PASS" and result["review_context"] == "independent_same_model"
    assert result["execution_mode"] == "mock" and len(model.requests) == 6
    request = model.requests[-1]
    assert request.tools is None and request.budget_context.purpose == "independent_reviewer"
    with store.connection() as connection:
        connection.execute("BEGIN")
        row = connection.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_runs WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)).fetchone()
        current = _packet(store, connection, row)
        assert current["artifacts"][0]["content"] == compact
        assert current["receipts"][0] == packet["receipts"][0]
        assert result["packet_sha256"] == _hash(current) != _hash(packet)
        history = [
            json.loads(item[0])["content"]
            for item in connection.execute(
                "SELECT parameters_json FROM action_intents WHERE tool_name IN ('file_write','file_revise') ORDER BY rowid"
            )
        ]
        assert history == [_json(content), _json(compact)]
        assert service._rounds(connection, worker["id"]) == 2


def test_immutable_receipts_exceeding_cap_cannot_get_capacity_revision(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

def seeded(tmp_path, *, chars=1500):
    store, manager, _model, worker = prepared(tmp_path, [])
    token = manager._claim(worker["id"])
    originals = {}
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        for ordinal in range(2, 10):
            message = {
                "role": "assistant",
                "content": f"original-{ordinal}:"
                + "x" * (chars if ordinal < 8 else 10)
                + "中文\r\n",
            }
            originals[ordinal] = message
            work.connection.execute(
                "INSERT INTO worker_messages VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
                (worker["id"], ordinal, message["role"], _json(message)),
            )
    return store, manager, worker, token, originals


def archives(store):
    with store.connection() as connection:
        return [tuple(row) for row in connection.execute("SELECT * FROM context_archives")]


def test_worker_batches_use_complete_previous_handoff_and_immutable_sources(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS", "false")
    store, manager, worker, token, originals = seeded(tmp_path)
    summaries, selected = [], []

    def handler(request):
        body = json.loads(request.content)
        assert not body.get("tools") and not body.get("response_format")
        assert len(json.dumps(body, ensure_ascii=False).encode()) + 64 + 128 <= 7000
        packet = json.loads(body["messages"][1]["content"])
        assert packet["previous_context"] == (summaries[-1] if summaries else {})
        for item in packet["messages"]:
            assert item["message"] == originals[item["ordinal"]]
            selected.append(item["ordinal"])
        summaries.append(f"Handoff {len(summaries) + 1}: preserve original analysis and next step.")
        return http_response(summaries[-1])

    gateway = mock_gateway(store, handler)
    manager.providers = ProviderPool({"protocol": gateway})
    compactor = WorkerModelCompactor(
        manager, gateway, worker["id"], token, context_limit=7000, output_limit=128
    )
    while True:
        result = asyncio.run(compactor.compact(input_budget=6000, source_readback_available=True))
        if not result["source_count"]:
            break
    assert len(summaries) >= 2 and selected == sorted(set(selected))
    assert selected[0] == 2 and selected[-1] <= 7
    service = ContextService(store)
    for ordinal in selected:
        assert (
            json.loads(service.read_source("worker", worker["id"], ordinal)["message_json"])
            == originals[ordinal]
        )
    context = service.build_worker_context(worker["id"], input_budget=6000)
    capsule = json.loads(
        next(
            item["content"] for item in context if item["content"].startswith("Archived task")
        ).split(": ", 1)[1]
    )
    assert capsule["model_handoff"]["text"] == summaries[-1]
    assert capsule["model_handoff"]["status"] == "unverified"
    assert capsule["task"]["task_node_key"] == "n"
    assert manager.get(worker["id"])["steps"] == len(summaries)
    assert manager.get(worker["id"])["token_spent"] == 40 * len(summaries)
    with store.connection() as c:
        local = c.execute("SELECT * FROM worker_model_reservations").fetchall()
        attempts = c.execute("SELECT * FROM model_budget_attempts").fetchall()
        assert len(local) == len(attempts) == len(summaries)
        assert all(
            row["state"] == "settled"
            and json.loads(row["context_json"])["purpose"] == "context_compaction"
            for row in local
        )
        assert all(
            row["purpose"] == "context_compaction" and row["worker_run_id"] == worker["id"]
            for row in attempts
        )
        assert c.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM evidence").fetchone()[0] == 0
    with store.unit_of_work() as work:
        work.connection.execute(
            "UPDATE worker_messages SET message_json='{}' WHERE run_id=? AND ordinal=2",
            (worker["id"],),
        )
    with pytest.raises(DomainError, match="integrity"):
        service.build_worker_context(worker["id"], input_budget=6000)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("race", ["expired", "new_owner", "paused", "plan", "capsule", "message"])
def test_worker_model_handoff_cannot_checkpoint_after_fence_or_frontier_changes(
    tmp_path, race, monkeypatch
):
    monkeypatch.setenv("FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS", "false")
    store, manager, worker, token, _originals = seeded(tmp_path)
    before = archives(store)

    def handler(_request):
        with store.unit_of_work() as work:
            if race == "expired":
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE worker_runs SET lease_until=0 WHERE id=?", (worker["id"],)
                )
            elif race == "new_owner":
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE worker_runs SET lease_token='REDACTED',generation=generation+1 WHERE id=?",
                    (worker["id"],),
                )
            elif race == "paused":
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE quests SET status='paused' WHERE id=?", (worker["quest_id"],)
                )
            elif race == "plan":
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE quest_plans SET status='superseded' WHERE id=?", (worker["plan_id"],)
                )
            elif race == "capsule":
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE worker_capsules SET revision=revision+1,next_action='changed' WHERE run_id=?",
                    (worker["id"],),
                )
            else:
                work.connection.execute(
                    "UPDATE worker_messages SET message_json=? WHERE run_id=? AND ordinal=2",
                    (_json({"role": "assistant", "content": "changed"}), worker["id"]),
                )
        return http_response()

    gateway = mock_gateway(store, handler)
    with pytest.raises(DomainError):
        asyncio.run(
            WorkerModelCompactor(
                manager, gateway, worker["id"], token, context_limit=9000, output_limit=128
            ).compact(input_budget=6000, source_readback_available=True)
        )
    assert archives(store) == before
    with store.connection() as c:
        # Received usage is settled even when it grants no checkpoint authority.
        assert c.execute("SELECT state FROM model_budget_attempts").fetchone()[0] == "settled"
        assert c.execute("SELECT state FROM worker_model_reservations").fetchone()[0] == "settled"
    assert manager.get(worker["id"])["token_spent"] == 40

import asyncio

def approved_report(
    tmp_path, *, criterion, files=None, successor=True, objective=None, source="source"
):
    files = files or {}
    store = Store(tmp_path / "core.sqlite3", workspace=Workspace.from_path(tmp_path))
    (tmp_path / "work").mkdir()
    (tmp_path / "work/input.txt").write_bytes(source.encode("utf-8"))
    objective = (
        objective or "Provide cited research findings, limitations and downstream-required fields."
    )
    quest = Quest(title="Report guidance fixture", goal=objective)
    store.save_quest(quest)
    nodes = [
        {
            "key": "research",
            "objective": objective,
            "success_criteria": [criterion],
            "budget_tokens": 60000,
            "allowed_tools": ["file_read", "file_write"],
        }
    ]
    if successor:
        nodes.append(
            {
                "key": "consumer",
                "objective": "Independently inspect the complete predecessor result.",
                "success_criteria": ["delivery_review"],
                "budget_tokens": 60000,
                "allowed_tools": ["file_read"],
            }
        )
    graphs = QuestGraphService(store)
    plan = graphs.propose(
        quest.id,
        {
            "nodes": nodes,
            "edges": [{"source": "research", "target": "consumer", "condition": "success"}]
            if successor
            else [],
            "max_total_tokens": 60000 * len(nodes),
        },
        expected_version=0,
    )
    graphs.approve(quest.id, plan["digest"], 1, expected_version=1, actor="local_user")
    store.save_model(
        ModelProfile(
            id="protocol",
            provider="protocol",
            model_id="fixture",
            display_name="Offline report fixture",
            context_window=64000,
            max_output_tokens=4000,
            tool_calling_support=ProtocolSupport(supported=True, source="test_fixture"),
        )
    )
    roles = [
        {
            "id": "coding" if index == 0 else "reviewer",
            "task_node_key": node["key"],
            "tools": node["allowed_tools"],
            "input_tokens": 30000,
            "output_tokens": 3000,
            "max_steps": 12,
            "max_tool_calls": 5,
            "max_duration_seconds": 120,
        }
        for index, node in enumerate(nodes)
    ]
    teams = TeamCompositionService(store)
    team = teams.propose(
        quest.id,
        roles,
        {
            "max_members": len(nodes),
            "max_depth": 0,
            "max_concurrency": 1,
            "max_total_tokens": 33000 * len(nodes),
            "max_total_tool_calls": 5 * len(nodes),
            "allowed_tools": ["file_read", "file_write"],
        },
        strategy="greedy",
        expected_version=2,
    )
    teams.approve(quest.id, 1, team["proposal_digest"], expected_version=2, actor="local_user")
    GovernanceService(store).grant_workspace(quest.id, "work", "local_user")
    model = ProtocolModel(
        [tool("file_read", {"path": "work/input.txt"})]
        + [
            tool("file_write", {"path": path, "content": content}, index + 2)
            for index, (path, content) in enumerate(files.items())
        ]
        + [response(delivery())]
    )
    manager = WorkerManager(
        store, ProviderPool({"protocol": model}), ToolEngine(store), team_authority=teams
    )
    worker = manager.start(
        quest.id, plan["id"], "research", team_digest=team["proposal_digest"], member_index=0
    )
    return store, manager, model, worker, plan

def test_complete_code_and_original_receipt_content_survive_guidance_and_reopen(tmp_path):
    source = 'original source "evidence" 中文\n' * 350
    code = "# Required complete implementation\n" + "# preserve every requested line\n" * 350
    code += "def result():\n    return 42\n"
    findings = json.dumps(
        {
            "conclusion": "Return 42 from the complete assigned implementation.",
            "source_path": "work/input.txt",
            "source_sha256": hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest(),
            "limitations": ["No execution result is claimed."],
            "downstream_fields": {"implementation": "work/complete.py", "expected_result": 42},
        }
    )
    store, manager, model, worker, _plan = approved_report(
        tmp_path,
        criterion="json_review:work/findings.json",
        files={"work/complete.py": code, "work/findings.json": findings},
        source=source,
        objective="Deliver the complete required code in full and a concise findings JSON for the next node.",
    )
    assert asyncio.run(manager.run(worker["id"]))["state"] == "review_pending"
    instruction = model.requests[0].messages[0]["content"]
    assert "never a size limit or permission to omit required material" in instruction
    assert "complete code, source reproductions" in instruction
    assert "downstream-required field once" in instruction
    assert (
        len(code.encode()) > 6144 and (tmp_path / "work/complete.py").read_bytes() == code.encode()
    )
    assert (tmp_path / "work/findings.json").read_bytes() == findings.encode()
    reopened = Store(store.path, workspace=store.workspace)
    with reopened.connection() as connection:
        persisted = json.loads(
            connection.execute(
                "SELECT message_json FROM worker_messages WHERE run_id=? AND ordinal=0",
                (worker["id"],),
            ).fetchone()[0]
        )
        receipts = [
            (row["tool_name"], json.loads(row["result_json"]))
            for row in connection.execute(
                "SELECT i.tool_name,r.result_json FROM action_receipts r "
                "JOIN action_intents i ON i.id=r.intent_id ORDER BY i.rowid"
            )
        ]
    assert persisted["content"] == instruction
    assert receipts[0][1]["content"] == source
    assert receipts[1][1]["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(code.encode()).hexdigest()
    assert receipts[2][1]["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(findings.encode()).hexdigest()
    assert manager.get(worker["id"])["tool_spent"] == 3
